scope: Current-date topic discovery of an untracked non-incretin weight-management programme; added to the existing open discovery review and not to the live catalogue.

candidate.name: ABBV-295 / GUB014295
candidate.stage: Completed Phase 1 study; sponsor says advancement into Phase 2 is planned
candidate.summary: AbbVie's 30 September 2026 announcement reports detailed multiple-ascending-dose Phase 1 findings for subcutaneous ABBV-295, an investigational long-acting amylin analogue. The sponsor says the findings support advancement into Phase 2 for chronic weight management; this is a planned next stage, not a completed Phase 2 trial.
candidate.formulation: Subcutaneous injection; weekly, every-other-week and monthly regimens were evaluated in parts of the Phase 1 study. Those schedules are research regimens, not authorised dosing.
candidate.ukAuthorisation: The sponsor states that ABBV-295 has not been approved by any health regulatory authority worldwide. The reviewed evidence therefore does not establish UK marketing authorisation.
candidate.nhsEngland: No NHS access is established by the reviewed evidence. The NICE name search produced unrelated fuzzy matches and cannot establish an appraisal or access route.
candidate.supply: No lawful UK retail supply or pharmacy stock is established. A UK Phase 1 research location is not evidence of commercial supply.
candidate.limitations: Early, sponsor-reported results from a small Phase 1 study whose primary objective was safety and tolerability. The detailed conference presentation was not independently reviewed here. Safety and efficacy are not established, and cross-trial efficacy comparisons are not supported.

sources.title: AbbVie: detailed Phase 1 ABBV-295 data at EASD 2026
sources.assessment: The complete sponsor response was read. It identifies the programme as investigational, describes 60 participants in Parts 2B/2C and 76 participants in the multiple-ascending-dose study overall, and expressly says ABBV-295 is not approved and its safety and efficacy are not established. Sponsor-reported weight and tolerability observations are not treated as approval or comparative effectiveness.

registry.title: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT06144684 (GUC17-01)
registry.assessment: The 15 January 2026 registry version records the first-in-human study as completed with 76 actual participants and a UK study location. It does not record a Phase 2 study, marketing authorisation, NHS access or retail supply.

regulatoryAccessChecks.result: The public URL returned the generic substance-search page without a name-specific result; absence could not be conclusively verified from that response. The sponsor's worldwide-not-approved statement is retained as the bounded evidence.

The site rewrote the query to a fuzzy term and returned unrelated results. It did not establish ABBV-295 guidance or NHS access, and the search is recorded as inconclusive rather than a definitive negative.

nextAction: Editorially assess whether ABBV-295 belongs in the live research summaries. Before any publication, look for a registered Phase 2 study or later sponsor confirmation, preserve the distinction between completed Phase 1 and planned Phase 2, and do not infer UK authorisation, NHS access or supply.
